skill.name: reactive-form-input

content.user_title: Verify Reactive Form Inputs Without Submitting
content.value_statement: A form can display the expected value while application state or validation remains unchanged. This skill guides evidence-based checks and reports input acceptance without submitting the form.
actual_capabilities: Guides identification of the visible, editable field within its current page and parent form, excluding hidden duplicates.
Separates displayed values from field-specific validation, dependent controls, and application state evidence.
Classifies input as effective, not effective, validating, or unverified using the available evidence.
Defines one bounded next observation with an expected completion signal or a clear stopping point.
Produces structured records from live observations or supplied notes while distinguishing proposed actions from completed interactions.
Requires sensitive value masking, normal input methods, and stopping before final form submission or request replay.
limitations: Provides workflow instructions and examples, not an executable browser automation tool or test suite.
Requires authorized browser access and suitable tools for live checks; supplied notes alone cannot establish unobserved application state.
Does not implement validation logic, repair application state synchronization, or confirm successful business submission.
Cannot confirm acceptance without a relevant application signal and must stop if further evidence requires final submission.

use_cases.title: Check Controlled Input Acceptance
use_cases.description: Separate a displayed contact value from the application model and identify whether normal input needs another authorized check.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers investigating controlled input synchronization

use_cases.title: Assess Pending Validation
use_cases.description: Record a workspace slug availability check, preserve the requested value, and observe within a fixed budget without creating the workspace.
use_cases.target_user: QA engineers testing asynchronous form validation

use_cases.title: Summarize Supplied Form Evidence
use_cases.description: Turn page notes into an input effectiveness record that names missing evidence and avoids claiming a live interaction occurred.
use_cases.target_user: Support analysts preparing form issue reports

prompt_templates.title: Interpret a Visible Value
prompt_templates.prompt: The contact email field looks filled, but I have no validation evidence. Classify what is known without browser access or submission. Name the missing evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Correct Field
prompt_templates.prompt: The profile form has a visible contact field, a hidden duplicate, and a similar header search. Plan an authorized check of the visible field. Specify replacement behavior and evidence needed without submitting.

prompt_templates.title: Observe Asynchronous Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: The workspace slug matches the requested value and shows Checking availability. In the authorized browser session, observe for at most five seconds. Report the last field-specific state without changing the slug or creating the workspace.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: bound a pending validation check

prompt_templates.title: Assess Evidence After Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: The supplied notes describe a DOM write before navigation and a disabled Save button afterward. The button depends on several fields. Produce an evidence record distinguishing page contexts, supplied observations, and proposed actions. Name one bounded next check without saving or replaying requests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: resolve stale context and ambiguous dependencies

output_examples.input: Supplied inspection: the visible contact email matches, its model is empty, and no validation is pending. Saving is prohibited.
output: Target: the visible Contact email field in the Profile form; hidden duplicates are excluded.
Display: the supplied inspection reports a matching value after DOM assignment; the sensitive value is masked.
Application signal: the same inspection reports an empty field model with no validation pending.
Conclusion: not effective in the supplied observation; no live interaction was performed.
Next: propose one normal keyboard replacement, then observe within the authorized test window for acceptance or a settled rejection.

output_examples.input: The workspace slug display matches, availability validation is pending, and the observation budget is five seconds.
output: Target: the visible Slug field in the current New workspace form.
Application signal: Checking availability is associated with that field; acceptance is not yet established.
Next: observe for up to five seconds, stopping on Available, a settled rejection, or expiry.
Keep the requested slug and report the last observed state if the budget expires.

output_examples.input: Only a screenshot shows a filled field and disabled Save button. No field validation or application model evidence is available.
output: Source: supplied screenshot only; no live check was performed.
Display: a value is visible, but application acceptance is not established.
Conclusion: unverified; the disabled button alone does not identify this field as the cause.
Gap: a field-specific application signal from the same page context.
Next: request a current validation observation for the target field without submitting.

best_practices: Record the page context, parent form, visible field identity, expected format, and replacement method before evaluating acceptance.
Mask sensitive values and distinguish live observations, supplied notes, and proposed actions.
Use field-specific signals with a bounded observation window, and stop before final submission or replay.
anti_patterns: Treating a DOM assignment or matching display as proof that the application accepted the input.
Using a disabled button alone to reject a field, or reporting pending validation as a settled failure.
Force-enabling controls, silently changing the requested value, or submitting the form to obtain more evidence.

faq.question: What problem does this skill address?
faq.answer: It checks whether a visible form value has supporting application acceptance evidence rather than relying on appearance alone.

faq.question: Does it include a browser automation tool?
faq.answer: No. It supplies a workflow, report template, examples, and checklist. Live checks require authorized access and separate browser tools.

faq.question: Can it work without browser access?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize supplied notes and report missing evidence, but it must not claim unperformed interactions or unobserved acceptance.

faq.question: What result states can it report?
faq.answer: It reports effective, not effective, validating, or unverified, with supporting evidence and any remaining gaps.

faq.question: Will it submit the business form?
faq.answer: No. It stops when further evidence requires final submission and does not replay an earlier uncertain request.

faq.question: Is a disabled Save button proof that the input failed?
faq.answer: No. The button may depend on other fields. A settled rejection or observed state mismatch must relate to the target field.
